To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the probability of error for minimum Hamming distance (MHD) fusion can be upper bounded for any finite number N of sensors, (2) the MHD fusion error tends to zero as N tends to infinity, and (3) the probability of the MHD fusion is a function of the pairwise Hamming distances between the code vectors and is independent of the code vectors themselves.

the fault-tolerance of a DCFEC code is determined by the minimum Hamming distances of the code, and a simple code design criterion based on the minimum Hamming weights of the code can be adopted to achieve the same fault-tolerance capability as the optimal code.

(i) the minimum Hamming Distance (HD) Fusion Error (MDFE) is a good criterion to design codes for DCFECC, (ii) the MDFE is a monotonically decreasing function of HD, and (iii) the MDFEs of codes with HDs close to the maximum possible HD are very close to zero
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a DCF ECC code with a given minimum Hamming distance for wireless sensor networks with a large number of sensors.
the performance analysis and code search of a minimum Hamming distance classification fusion code for a network with a large number of sensors.
the performance analysis and code design for the DCFECC with minimum Hamming fusion.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the new code design criterion proposed in this paper can be used to construct DCFECC codes for wireless sensor networks with a desired fault-tolerance level and a complexity much less than that of the minimum Hamming fusion error criterion.

the new code search criterion of less complexity can be used to construct DCFECC codes for networks with a large number of sensors that perform almost identically to those found based on the minimum Hamming fusion error criterion, but at a fraction of complexity.
the code design based on the new code search criterion is a very good choice for the DCFECC scheme.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have established a solid mathematical basis for DCFECC, which can be used to construct codes with the desired fault tolerance capability for a network of any given size.

the performance of DCFECC codes can be analyzed and the codes can be designed based on the pair-wise Hamming distance of the codes, and this is a much less complex approach than the minimum Haming distance fusion error criterion.

we have established a complete performance analysis and a code design for the DCFECC codes with minimum Hamming Distance fusion, and have proposed a code search criterion that is much simpler than the minimum Haming distance fusion error criterion, and yet performs almost identically.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the minimum Hamming code distance fusion error is a good criterion in searching for a DCFECK code with good performance in wireless sensor networks.

, with the new code design criterion, a network with over 100 sensors can have a fault-tolerance capability comparable to that of a network with over ten sensors, if the code is constructed based on the minimum Hamming fusion error criterion.
, in the design of DCFECC codes, the code length is not necessarily a critical parameter.
